args.title: checkout-api v2.3.1 failing health checks; rolled back to v2.3.0
args.summary: After the deploy of checkout-api v2.3.1 to all production regions (us-east, us-west, eu-west), the service failed health checks with an error rate of ~18%. v2.3.1 was also unhealthy in staging as v2.3.1-rc. Action taken: rolled checkout-api back in all regions to v2.3.0, the most recent release that was healthy in production. After the rollback, all regions are on v2.3.0, the service reports healthy, and the error rate is ~0.2%. Follow-up: find the root cause of the v2.3.1 failure, and find out why a release that was unhealthy in staging was promoted to production.

trace.final:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's passing health checks again. I also opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001), which paged the on-call engineer.

1. **What I found:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with about an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. v2.3.1 had also been unhealthy in staging (as v2.3.1-rc), but it was still released to production.
2. **Rollback:** After moving all three regions to v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is down to about 0.2%. No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
3. **Incident:** INC-0001 covers the failure, the rollback and the result. It lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and why a release that was unhealthy in staging reached production. My first attempt to create the incident timed out. I checked that nothing had been created before retrying, and used the same duplicate-protection key both times, so there's only one incident.

content.text: Most recent healthy production release is v2.3.0.

content.text:
I rolled checkout-api back to v2.3.0 in all three regions, and it's passing health checks again. I also opened a SEV2 incident (INC-0001), which paged the on-call engineer.

1. **What I found:** v2.3.1 was running in us-east, us-west and eu-west, failing health checks with about an 18% error rate. v2.3.0 was the most recent release that had been healthy in production. v2.3.1 had also been unhealthy in staging (as v2.3.1-rc), but it was still released to production.
2. **Rollback:** After moving all three regions to v2.3.0, the service reports healthy and the error rate is down to about 0.2%. No approval was needed, because v2.3.0 had already been healthy in production.
3. **Incident:** INC-0001 covers the failure, the rollback and the result. It lists two follow-ups: find out why v2.3.1 failed, and why a release that was unhealthy in staging reached production. My first attempt to create the incident timed out. I checked that nothing had been created before retrying, and used the same duplicate-protection key both times, so there's only one incident.
